title: Affine and stalk comparison for coherent reflexive modules
statement: Let $Y$ be an integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] and $F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $F^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_Y}(F,\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. A module $N$ over a commutative ring $A$ is reflexive when evaluation $N\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(\operatorname{Hom}_A(N,A),A)$ is an isomorphism. Then the following are equivalent: (i) the sheaf evaluation $F\to F^{\vee\vee}$ is an isomorphism; (ii) for every affine open $W\subseteq Y$, $F(W)$ is a reflexive $\mathcal O_Y(W)$-module; (iii) for every point $y\in Y$, $F_y$ is a reflexive $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-module, with stalk as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. In particular for a Noetherian domain $A$ and a finite $A$-module $M$, the associated coherent sheaf $\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] is reflexive if and only if $M$ is reflexive.

source.place: Tags 0AY0 (divisors-lemma-check-reflexive-on-affines) and 0AY3 (divisors-lemma-check-reflexive). The last sentence is the affine specialization, using the finite-module associated sheaf.

proof.text: First $\mathcal O_Y$ is coherent. On every affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] with rank one identifies $\mathcal O_W$ with $\widetilde A$, so $\mathcal O_Y$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-def-coherent]. It is of finite type, generated by $1$ on every open. Apply [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Open subschemes remain locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], and coherent modules restrict to coherent modules by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover](1). These observations apply to all affine opens used below, including the empty open.

For any coherent module $H$ on $Y$, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-hom-local-kernel] expresses $H^\vee$ locally as a kernel of a map between finite sums of $\mathcal O_Y$. Those sums and kernels are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum](1),(3); coherence glues by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover](2). Apply this first to $H=F$ and then to $H=F^\vee$. Thus $F,F^\vee,F^{\vee\vee}$ are coherent and hence quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Moreover $F$ and $F^\vee$ are of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-local-finite-presentation]: at each point its finite free cokernel presentation is exactly the condition of [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](2). Sheaf Hom restricts to sheaf Hom on each open, directly from its definition [def-pur-sheaf-hom].

Fix an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and write $M=F(W)$. For a quasi-coherent module $H$ on $W$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1),(3) identifies $H$ with $\widetilde{H(W)}$ and gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_W}(H,\mathcal O_W)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(H(W),A)$. The bijection takes a sheaf morphism $\varphi$ to its section map $\varphi_W$, as follows from the stated adjunction formula and the counit corresponding to the identity. It is $A$-linear because addition and scalar multiplication of morphisms are sectionwise. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom], applying this to $F|_W$ gives $F^\vee(W)\cong M^*$, where $M^*=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,A)$. Applying it to $F^\vee|_W$ and precomposing with the inverse of this isomorphism gives $F^{\vee\vee}(W)\cong M^{**}$. Under these isomorphisms the section map of evaluation $e:F\to F^{\vee\vee}$ is $M\to M^{**}$: for $s\in F(W)$ and $\varphi\in F^\vee(W)$ its value is $\varphi_W(s)$, by the definition of evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0AY0 (lemma-check-reflexive-on-affines), omitted proof expanded using Tags 01I6 (section-quasi-coherent-affine) and 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions)

proof.text: If $e$ is an isomorphism, each $e_W$ is an isomorphism, so step 3 proves (ii). Conversely, assume (ii). Step 3 says $e_W$ is an isomorphism for every affine open $W$. Both $F|_W$ and $F^{\vee\vee}|_W$ are quasi-coherent by step 2, so the natural counits of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) identify $e|_W$ with $\widetilde{e_W}$; it is therefore an isomorphism. The inverses on the affine cover agree on every overlap because both invert $e$ there. By [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules](1) they glue to an inverse of $e$, and the two inverse identities can be checked on that cover. This proves (i) if and only if (ii). In particular, on a single affine scheme it suffices that evaluation on global sections is an isomorphism.

Fix $y\in Y$ and put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. Since $F$ and $F^\vee$ are finitely presented by step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-finite-presentation] gives canonical linear isomorphisms $c:(F^\vee)_y\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_y,R)$ and $d:(F^{\vee\vee})_y\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_R((F^\vee)_y,R)$. Precomposing $d$ with $c^{-1}$ identifies the latter target with $\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_y,R),R)$. This identifies $e_y$ with module evaluation: given $s_y\in F_y$ and $\psi\in\operatorname{Hom}_R(F_y,R)$, surjectivity of $c$ writes $\psi=c(\varphi_y)$ for a germ of a local sheaf morphism $\varphi$. Represent $s_y$ and $\varphi_y$ on a common neighbourhood. By [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-internal-hom-evaluation], the image of $e_y(s_y)$ evaluated on $\psi$ is $(\varphi(s))_y=\psi(s_y)$. Thus the comparison preserves the actual evaluation map, not merely the two double-dual objects.

source.place: Tag 0AY3 (lemma-check-reflexive), equivalence of (1) and (2); Tag 01CP (lemma-stalk-internal-hom), canonical-map formula

proof.text: By step 5, condition (iii) says exactly that $e_y$ is bijective for every point $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] this is equivalent to $e$ being an isomorphism. This proves (i) if and only if (iii), and together with step 4 proves the three-way equivalence.

Finally let $A$ be a Noetherian domain and $M$ a finite $A$-module. The scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian by the one-chart definition [pqf-def-locnoeth], and integral by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2). The associated sheaf $\widetilde M$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] and has global sections $M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](2). It is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Step 3 identifies its evaluation on global sections with $M\to M^{**}$. The single-affine conclusion of step 4 therefore proves that $\widetilde M$ is reflexive exactly when $M$ is reflexive. When $M=0$ all the evaluation maps are the unique isomorphisms of zero modules; on an empty affine open the sheaf modules and their duals are likewise zero, so no exception to the assertions is needed.

The statement keeps the source hypotheses (integral, locally Noetherian, coherent). (i)⇔(ii) is 0AY0 and (i)⇔(iii) is 0AY3 (1)⇔(2); the closed-point clause is not asserted and nothing is weakened. This is not a re-split: the delivery has no new nodes and turns an empty proof into 7 steps. Step 1: O_Y is coherent by the rank-1 tilde-free node, generation by 1 and 01XZ; restriction to opens is covered. Step 2: the duals are coherent by coherent-hom-local-kernel with target O, kernel-cokernel-sum (1),(3) and local-on-open-cover (2); finite presentation comes from coherent-local-finite-presentation. Step 3: under adjunction (1),(3), φ maps to φ_W because ε_W∘τ_W=id, and e_W is M→M** (checked by hand). Step 4: counit naturality makes e|_W an isomorphism; the inverses glue by glue (1), which also gives the single-affine variant. Step 5: c and d are isomorphisms by the finite-presentation node; two applications of the evaluation formula show d(e_y(s_y))(φ_y)=c(φ_y)(s_y). Step 6: module-iso-on-stalks. Step 7: Spec A is integral and locally Noetherian, M~ is quasi-coherent, of finite type by (a) with Γ=M, hence coherent. Edge cases checked: M=0, A^n, A/(a), the conductor example over k[t^2,t^3], and the empty open. rg found no duplicate for reflexive or 0AY0/0AY3. All 12 declared tool_uses, generic off-unit sheaf and module foundations used exactly as stated, are accepted. No SGA source is cited and no fixes were made.

lean.statement: theorem affine_stalk_reflexive_module_comparison (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral Y] [IsLocallyNoetherian Y] (F : Y.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent Y.toRingedSpace F) : (IsIso (SheafOfModules.bidual (R := Y.sheaf) F) ↔ ∀ (W : Y.Opens), IsAffineOpen W → Module.IsReflexive Γ(Y, W) Γ(F, W)) ∧ (IsIso (SheafOfModules.bidual (R := Y.sheaf) F) ↔ ∀ (y : Y), Module.IsReflexive (Y.presheaf.stalk y) ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y.toRingedSpace y).obj F))
